title: Uniform mass of each disjoint-model fiber
statement:
Fix an integer $n \ge 1$, and equip the finite space of hard samples with its uniform probability measure: a hard sample records a special coordinate $T \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, two bits $x_T, y_T$, and a disjoint-coordinate value at each of the $n$ coordinates, so there are $n\cdot 4\cdot 3^{\,n}$ of them, each carrying mass $1/(n\cdot 4\cdot 3^{\,n})$. Then for every point $z$ of the space $\{1,\dots,n\}\times\big(\{1,\dots,n\}\to \text{DisjointCoordinate}\big)\times \text{DisjointCoordinate}$, the set of hard samples that lie in the disjointness event and whose disjoint model equals $z$ has measure exactly
\[
\frac{1}{n\cdot 4\cdot 3^{\,n}},
\]
the mass of a single sample.
hypotheses_covered: z an arbitrary point of the disjoint-model space Fin n × (Fin n → DisjointCoordinate) × DisjointCoordinate
measure is the uniform measure on the finite hard-sample space
replaced: Under the hard distribution, a singleton fiber of the disjoint model together with $D$ has one ambient sample's worth of mass.
